items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I became quite friendly with the first trumpet player in Joy's orchestra whose name was Flo Dreyer. They were still touring when I returned to the States and I used to send Flo 'Down Beat' magazines and other journals concerning jazz musicians. So Flo sent me a nice Zippo cigarette lighter from Hong

ctx.x: When I arrived in Paris, I had exactly one hundred dollars but as Serge had advanced me some francs on my weekly salary, I didn't have to change any dollars and decided to buy some American Express checks. But I kept delaying this procedure and when I went out, I would hide the money somewhere in my room so that if something happened when I was out, the money would not be in my pockets. One day, I decided to have a blue suit cleaned and gave it to a cleaning place on the rue Pigalle. Two days later, I was looking…

I seemed to have had a losing streak for a certain time because shortly after the loss of my money, I lost a slave bracelet that was given to me by the U.S. Coast guard Training station in appreciation for a concert I did at the base in St. Alban, New York, with the Ellis Larkins trio. There was an all girl orchestra on a tour in the Philippines by the name of Joy Cayler. I spoke to Joy before when mentioning the different groups that were doing U.S.A. shows. I became quite friendly with the first trumpet player…

One night, I went to the club with some of the musicians from the Eduoard's band and after a few drinks, I felt like blowing, so I joined the musicians that were playing and I happened to have my axe with me. I felt like smoking also so I lit a cigarette. I never laid a cigarette on a piano or anything else that tood the fisk of being burned, so I took my lighter and laid it on the piano and put my cigarette on it when I was blowing my horn. I never saw the lighter after that.
